quarterly_data.quarter: Shin-Etsu Chemical results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2027 telephone conference summary (07-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: President Yasuhiko Saitoh (Q1 telephone conference summary, quarter ended June 30, 2026): consolidated net sales JPY 662.4 billion (up 5.4% year on year), operating income JPY 173.7 billion (up 4.2%), ordinary income JPY 192.1 billion (up 5.8%), net income attributable to owners of parent JPY 130.8 billion (up 3.5%); earnings per share up 6% to JPY 70.39. By segment: Electronics Materials is booming as a whole, with the advanced sector strong on the expanding AI-related market and ripple effects in other sectors; Functional Materials results of the strategy to raise sales of functional and specialty products are starting to show in the numbers; Processing & Specialized Services earnings are growing, mainly in semiconductor-related sectors.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 net sales JPY 662.4 billion (+5.4%); operating income JPY 173.7 billion (+4.2%); net income JPY 130.8 billion (+3.5%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Shin-Etsu Chemical results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2027 telephone conference summary (07-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Full-year forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027: President Saitoh said several factors still make the year hard to forecast; consolidated net sales JPY 2,700 billion (up 4.9%), operating income JPY 700 billion (up 10.2%), ordinary income JPY 770 billion (up 8.7%), net income attributable to owners of parent JPY 525.0 billion (up 10.7%), net income per share JPY 286 (up 13.2%). Saitoh said the company recognises the forecast falls short of analysts' expectations, attributes the gap to Infrastructure Materials, where it takes a cautious view, and will work to raise earnings in all segments. Corporate Officer Toshiyuki Kasahara: full-year investment and depreciation forecasts are unchanged from April; assumed exchange rates from July are about JPY 160 per US dollar and about JPY 180 per euro; ordinary-income FX sensitivity is JPY 3.7 billion per year for the US dollar and JPY 0.2 billion for the euro.
quarterly_data.figure: FY net sales JPY 2,700 billion (+4.9%); operating income JPY 700 billion (+10.2%); net income JPY 525.0 billion (+10.7%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Shin-Etsu Chemical results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2027 telephone conference summary (07-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Q1 telephone conference Q&A summary) on wafer supply: for 300 mm wafers all wafer manufacturers appear to be running at full capacity already and supply is increasingly constrained by their production capacity; the company expects the high demand to continue into Q2 and beyond, and also expects strong demand for 200 mm and smaller wafers, where it is running at full capacity in terms of personnel. President Saitoh said that in some cases devices that cannot be made because of a 300 mm wafer shortage are being made on 200 mm wafers instead, and that for many of its products, not only wafers, the company has received supply requests exceeding its current production capacity and is working to make the needed investments and set pricing that makes them viable. Dummy wafers for setting up new device lines and monitor wafers for process verification appear to be in shortage and management expects them to stay tight for some time; reclaimed wafers from group company Mimasu Semiconductor Industry, used as monitor wafers, are in much higher demand and that business is running at full capacity.

quarterly_data.quarter: Shin-Etsu Chemical results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2027 telephone conference summary (07-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Q1 telephone conference Q&A summary) on the silicon wafer market in Q1: the 300 mm market grew mid single digits year on year and high single digits quarter on quarter, with demand recovering rapidly from around June and 300 mm wafer shipments in June reaching a record monthly high; management attributes the recovery partly to a significant shift in customers' attitude to inventories after the situation in the Middle East and to customers planning expansions wanting inventory ahead of growing AI demand. The 200 mm market rose by the mid-teens both year on year and quarter on quarter; 150 mm and smaller rose high single digits year on year and mid-teens quarter on quarter, which management attributes to customers' falling wafer inventories and the start of a recovery in consumer-electronics and industrial-equipment demand.
quarterly_data.figure: 300 mm market up mid single digits YoY and high single digits QoQ; June 300 mm shipments a record monthly high; 200 mm up mid-teens YoY and QoQ

quarterly_data.quarter: Shin-Etsu Chemical results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2027 telephone conference summary (07-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Q1 telephone conference Q&A summary) on AI demand, long-term agreements (LTAs) and investment: device makers seem to be starting to believe AI demand is quite strong and will last a long time; AI behaves like infrastructure rather than a unit-count market, so running the business on firm contractual commitments matters more. Slightly less than 10% of 300 mm wafers go to devices that use two wafers, a share management expects to keep expanding. The most recent contracts were all signed around 2020-21 in the COVID-19 boom, and wafer makers appear quite cautious now; the company's LTA expiry dates vary by customer, with some expiring by the end of next year and others running another 3-4 years. Capital investment costs (construction, equipment, raw materials, transport, packaging) have risen sharply - management estimates simply building a new plant would cost more than twice its previous investment - so pricing must reflect this and it has no intention of rushing into investment; investment cost varies greatly by wafer type and technology level. The company already has an integrated US process from crystal growth to polished and epitaxial wafers, but has not decided where its next investment will be and will decide after weighing quality and cost.
quarterly_data.figure: Slightly less than 10% of 300 mm wafers for two-wafer devices; new plant cost more than twice the previous investment; LTAs expiring from end of next year to another 3-4 years

quarterly_data.quarter: Shin-Etsu Chemical results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2027 telephone conference summary (07-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Infrastructure Materials (Q1 telephone conference summary): President Saitoh said North American PVC domestic sales volume for April-June was up 12% from January-March and up 4% year on year (industry statistics), and the company passed on a price increase of 7 cents per pound over the March price in North America; overseas, price increases in place since the start of the year were rolled back in late May as Asian inventories rose more than expected and demand weakened, which he attributes mainly to a supply-side overreaction; Chinese firms began raising prices the week before. Caustic soda was relatively stable. Management on US subsidiary Shintech (December year-end, one quarter lag): ordinary income rose from the prior quarter but fell slightly year on year; the company is cautious on its second-half forecast; North American PVC demand is expected to settle at a good level, with housing not particularly strong but industrial, data-center and infrastructure investment stable and supporting demand; Shintech's costs have not changed significantly. In magnetic materials the company is working with customers on emergency measures to minimise heavy rare-earth use and on multiple measures for raw-material issues.
quarterly_data.figure: North American PVC domestic sales volume +12% QoQ, +4% YoY; price increase of 7 cents per pound
